subject: Further Mathematics
examFormat: Two papers, both of which must be taken. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice objective questions covering the entire syllabus, all to be answered in 1 1/2 hours for 40 marks (Pure Mathematics 30, Statistics and Probability 4, Vectors and Mechanics 6 questions). Paper 2: Sections A and B answered in 2 1/2 hours for 100 marks; Section A has eight compulsory elementary questions for 48 marks (Pure Mathematics 4, Statistics and Probability 2, Vectors and Mechanics 2); Section B has seven longer questions in three parts (Pure Mathematics 3, Statistics and Probability 2, Vectors and Mechanics 2), of which candidates answer four, with at least one from each part, for 52 marks. More challenging questions may also be set on topics in the General Mathematics (Core) syllabus.
excluded: Items marked with a single asterisk (topics peculiar to Ghana only) were left out: graphs of logarithmic functions (y = ax^b) and estimation of a and b, recurrence series, equation of the image of a line under a linear transformation, expressing a sin x + b cos x in the form R cos(x +/- alpha) or R sin(x +/- alpha), distance from an external point to a line, sketching parabolas and finding the axis of symmetry, position vector of a point dividing a line segment in the ratio lambda:mu, resultant of vectors by scale drawing, and the equation of the line of regression (least squares). Items marked with two asterisks (Nigeria only) were included. Units, calculator and equipment notes were skipped.

topics.name: Sets
objectives: Define a set by a property and use set notations and their meanings
Identify disjoint sets, the universal set and the complement of a set
Use Venn diagrams to solve problems, including three-set problems
Apply the commutative and associative laws and the distributive properties over union and intersection
Use De Morgan's laws to solve related problems
topics.content: More challenging problems involving union, intersection, the universal set, subset and complement of a set.

topics.name: Surds
objectives: Perform all four operations on surds of the form a/sqrt(n), a sqrt(b) and a + b sqrt(n), where a is rational, b is a positive integer and n is not a perfect square
Rationalise the denominators of such surds

topics.name: Binary Operations
objectives: State and use the properties of binary operations: closure, commutativity, associativity, distributivity, identity elements and inverses
Use these properties to solve related problems

topics.name: Logical Reasoning
objectives: Apply the rules of syntax: true or false statements, rules of logic applied to arguments, implications and deductions
Use logical reasoning to determine the validity of compound statements involving implications and connectives, using symbols such as ~P, p v q, p ^ q and p => q
Use truth tables to deduce conclusions of compound statements, including negation

topics.name: Functions
objectives: Define the domain and co-domain of a function, using notation such as f: x -> 3x + 4
Identify one-to-one, onto, identity and constant mappings
Represent a function graphically and identify the image and the range
Determine the inverse of a one-to-one function
Find the composite of functions, with the notation fog(x) = f(g(x))
topics.content: Restrict to simple algebraic functions only.

subtopics.name: Linear Functions, Equations and Inequalities
objectives: Recognise and sketch graphs of linear functions and equations
Use the gradient and intercept forms of linear equations, and conditions for parallel and perpendicular lines
Solve linear inequalities and represent linear inequalities in two variables graphically
Apply linear inequalities to linear programming

subtopics.name: Quadratic Functions, Equations and Inequalities
objectives: Recognise and sketch graphs of quadratic functions f: x -> ax^2 + bx + c
Identify the vertex, axis of symmetry, maximum and minimum, and increasing and decreasing parts of a parabola
Find values of x for which f(x) > 0 or f(x) < 0
Solve simultaneous equations, one linear and one quadratic
Solve quadratic equations by completing the squares and express f(x) in the form a(x + d)^2 + k
Classify the roots of a quadratic equation (equal, real and unequal, imaginary) using the discriminant
Use the sum and product of roots to form equations whose roots are related to the given roots
Solve quadratic inequalities

subtopics.name: Cubic Functions and Equations
objectives: Recognise cubic functions f: x -> ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d and draw their graphs for a given range
Factorise cubic expressions, including a^3 +/- b^3, and solve cubic equations
Perform basic operations on polynomials
Apply the remainder and factor theorems

topics.name: Rational Functions
objectives: Work with rational functions of the form Q(x) = f(x)/g(x), g(x) not equal to 0, where f(x) and g(x) are polynomials
Perform the four basic operations on rational functions and find zeros, domain and range (sketching not required)
Resolve rational functions into partial fractions
topics.content: g(x) may be factorised into linear and quadratic factors; the degree of the numerator is less than that of the denominator, which is less than or equal to 4.

subtopics.name: Indices
objectives: State and apply the laws of indices to evaluate products, quotients, powers and nth roots
Solve equations involving indices

subtopics.name: Logarithms
objectives: State and apply the laws of logarithms in calculations involving products, quotients, powers and nth roots
Solve equations involving logarithms, including change of base
Reduce a relation such as y = ax^b to linear form: log10 y = b log10 x + log10 a

topics.name: Permutation and Combinations
objectives: Solve simple cases of arrangements (permutations) and selections (combinations) of objects, e.g. arranging students in a row or drawing balls from a box with or without replacement
Use the notations nCr and nPr, with nPr = n!/(n-r)! and nCr = n!/(r!(n-r)!)

topics.name: Binomial Theorem
objectives: Expand (a + b)^n using the binomial theorem for positive integral index (proof not required)
Use (1 + x)^n approximately equal to 1 + nx for any rational n, where x is sufficiently small, e.g. (0.998)^(1/3)

topics.name: Sequences and Series
objectives: Distinguish between finite and infinite sequences and series
Recognise the pattern of a sequence; use the arithmetic progression (A.P.) Un = U1 + (n-1)d and the geometric progression (G.P.) Un = U1 r^(n-1)
Find the sum of an A.P.: Sn = n/2 (U1 + Un) or Sn = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d]
Find the sum of a G.P.: Sn = U1(1 - r^n)/(1 - r), r < 1, or Sn = U1(r^n - 1)/(r - 1), r > 1
Find the sum to infinity of a G.P., S = U1/(1 - r), |r| < 1

topics.name: Matrices and Linear Transformation
topics.content: Standard matrices include reflection in the x-axis [1 0; 0 -1], reflection in the y-axis [-1 0; 0 1], reflection in the line y = x [0 1; 1 0], anti-clockwise rotation through theta about the origin [cos theta, -sin theta; sin theta, cos theta], and the general matrix for reflection in a line through the origin making an angle theta with the positive x-axis.

subtopics.name: Matrices
objectives: State the order of a matrix and indicate its type
Use equality of matrices to find missing entries
Add and subtract matrices (up to 3 x 3)
Multiply a matrix by a scalar and by a matrix (up to 3 x 3)

subtopics.name: Determinants
objectives: Evaluate determinants of 2 x 2 matrices
Evaluate determinants of 3 x 3 matrices
Apply determinants to the solution of simultaneous linear equations

subtopics.name: Inverse of 2 x 2 Matrices
objectives: Find the inverse of a 2 x 2 matrix

subtopics.name: Linear Transformation
objectives: Find the images of points under a given linear transformation
Determine the matrices of given linear transformations
Find the inverse of a linear transformation (2 x 2 matrices) and the composition of linear transformations
Recognise the identity transformation

subtopics.name: Trigonometric Ratios and Rules
objectives: Find the sine, cosine and tangent of general angles (0 to 360 degrees)
Identify trigonometric ratios of 30, 45 and 60 degrees without tables
Use basic trigonometric ratios and reciprocals to prove given trigonometric identities
Evaluate the sine, cosine and tangent of negative angles
Convert degrees into radians and vice versa
Apply trigonometry to heights and distances, perimeters, solution of triangles, angles of elevation and depression, and bearings, including the sine and cosine rules

subtopics.name: Compound and Multiple Angles
objectives: Use sin(A +/- B), cos(A +/- B) and tan(A +/- B) in simple identities and in finding ratios such as sin 75 and cos 150 without tables, leaving answers as surds
Use simple trigonometric identities to find trigonometric ratios of compound and multiple angles (up to 3A)

subtopics.name: Trigonometric Functions and Equations
objectives: Relate trigonometric ratios to Cartesian coordinates of points (x, y) on the circle x^2 + y^2 = r^2
Draw and interpret graphs of sine, cosine, tangent and functions of the form a sin x + b cos x, identifying maximum and minimum points and increasing and decreasing portions
Solve simple trigonometric equations graphically, e.g. a sin x + b cos x = k
Solve trigonometric equations up to quadratic equations, e.g. 2 sin^2 x - sin x - 3 = 0, for 0 to 360 degrees

subtopics.name: Straight Lines
objectives: Find the mid-point of a line segment and the coordinates of points dividing a line in a given ratio
Find the distance between two points and the gradient of a line
Write the equation of a line in intercept form and gradient form
State the conditions for parallel and perpendicular lines
Calculate the acute angle between two intersecting lines

subtopics.name: Conic Sections
objectives: Determine loci of variable points which move under given conditions
Write the equation of a circle in terms of centre (a, b) and radius r, and in the general form x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0
Find tangents and normals to circles
Use the equation of a parabola in rectangular Cartesian coordinates (y^2 = 4ax), including parametric equations (at^2, at)
Find the equation of a tangent and normal to a parabola at a given point

topics.name: Differentiation
objectives: Explain the idea of a limit (intuitive treatment) and relate it to the gradient of a curve
Explain the meaning of the derivative of a function and determine it from first principles (simple cases only)
Differentiate polynomials
Differentiate trigonometric functions, e.g. sin x and a sin x +/- b cos x
Apply the product and quotient rules and differentiate implicit functions such as ax^2 + by^2 = c, including polynomials of the form (a + bx^n)^m
Differentiate transcendental functions, e.g. y = e^(ax), y = log 3x and y = ln x
Use second order derivatives, rates of change and small changes, and the concept of maxima and minima
Find the equation of a tangent to a curve at a point
Sketch curves (up to cubic functions) and solve linear kinematics problems
topics.content: Restrict turning points to maxima and minima.

subtopics.name: Indefinite Integral
objectives: Integrate polynomials of the form ax^n, n not equal to -1
Integrate sums and differences of polynomials
Integrate polynomials of the form ax^n with n = -1, i.e. the integral of 1/x dx = ln x
Solve simple problems on integration by substitution
Integrate simple trigonometric functions

subtopics.name: Definite Integral
objectives: Evaluate definite integrals and relate them to the area under a curve

subtopics.name: Applications of the Definite Integral
objectives: Find plane areas and rates of change, including linear kinematics
Find the volume of a solid of revolution
Use approximation restricted to the trapezium rule

subtopics.name: Tabulation and Graphical Representation of Data
objectives: Construct frequency tables and cumulative frequency tables
Draw histograms, including those with unequal class intervals
Draw the cumulative frequency curve (ogive) for grouped data

subtopics.name: Measures of Location
objectives: Determine mean, median, mode, quartiles and percentiles
Find the mode and modal group for grouped data from a histogram
Find the median from grouped data
Find the mean for grouped data (use of an assumed mean required)

subtopics.name: Measures of Dispersion
objectives: Determine the range, inter-quartile and semi inter-quartile range from an ogive
Determine mean deviation, variance and standard deviation for grouped and ungrouped data, using an assumed mean or true mean

subtopics.name: Correlation
objectives: Draw scatter diagrams and use the line of best fit to predict one variable from another
Explain the meaning of correlation: positive, negative and zero correlation
Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (data without ties)

topics.name: Probability
objectives: Explain the meaning of probability and relative frequency
Calculate probability using simple sample spaces, e.g. tossing 2 dice once or drawing from a box with or without replacement
Apply addition and multiplication of probabilities to equally likely, mutually exclusive, independent and conditional events, treating the probability of an event as the probability of a set
Use the binomial distribution P(x = r) = nCr p^r q^(n-r), where p + q = 1 (simple problems only)
Use the Poisson distribution P(x) = e^(-lambda) lambda^x / x!, where lambda = np, n is large and p is small

topics.name: Vectors
objectives: Define scalar and vector quantities and represent vectors, including in the form ai + bj
Perform algebra of vectors: addition, subtraction and multiplication of vectors by scalars, and state the commutative, associative and distributive properties
Use the triangle, parallelogram and polygon laws, and solve problems in elementary plane geometry, e.g. concurrency of medians and diagonals
Calculate unit vectors and use position vectors, including the position vector of the midpoint of a line segment
Resolve and compose vectors, e.g. find the resultant of forces acting at a point
Find the angle between two vectors and use the scalar (dot) product to establish trigonometric formulae such as cos(a +/- b), the cosine rule and the sine rule
Use the vector (cross) product and its application
topics.content: The unit vectors i and j lie along the x and y axes respectively; position vector of A relative to O is OA.

topics.name: Statics
objectives: Define a force and represent forces
Compose and resolve coplanar forces acting at a point
Compose and resolve general coplanar forces on rigid bodies
Apply conditions for equilibrium of bodies, e.g. suspension of particles by strings
Determine the resultant of forces and apply Lami's theorem
Use the principles of moments to solve related problems
Distinguish between smooth and rough planes and determine the coefficient of friction

topics.name: Dynamics
objectives: Define displacement, velocity, acceleration and speed and compose velocities and accelerations
Describe rectilinear motion and apply Newton's laws of motion, including motion along inclined planes and motion under gravity (ignoring air resistance)
Apply the equations of motion: v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at^2 and v^2 = u^2 + 2as
Apply conservation of linear momentum (excluding coefficient of restitution) and distinguish between momentum and impulse
Solve problems on projectiles (objects projected at an angle to the horizontal)
